title: Berger's effect in Python, from BIDS: occipital alpha blocks when the eyes open

dataset.name: EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb)
dataset.record: subject S001, baseline runs R01 (eyes open) and R02 (eyes closed), 64-channel EEG @ 160 Hz, written to a BIDS layout and read with physio.io.read_bids (mne-bids)
dataset.citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng. 2004;51(6):1034-43. Goldberger AL, et al. PhysioNet. Circulation. 2000;101(23):e215-20.

proposition: The Python side of the ecosystem (physiopy) reproduces Berger's classic finding from a BIDS recording: occipital (O1/Oz/O2) alpha power is about 14x higher with the eyes closed than open (eyes-closed 3.35e-09 vs eyes-open 2.32e-10 integrated band power; ratio 14.4), read end-to-end from native BIDS. The direction and ratio reproduce; absolute magnitudes are preprocessing-dependent.

claims.statement: occipital alpha, eyes closed (integrated band power)
occipital alpha, eyes open (integrated band power)

validation.reference: Berger's alpha-blocking effect (Berger, 1929) and the R eeg-berger-eegmmidb recipe in this same gallery, which reaches the identical conclusion from the same subject.
validation.data: REAL - PhysioNet eegmmidb subject S001 (baseline runs R01/R02), read from a BIDS layout via physio.io.read_bids.
validation.note: Single subject; the ~14x eyes-closed/eyes-open ratio and its direction are the robust finding. Absolute band-power magnitudes are preprocessing- and reference-dependent (not universal constants), and this is not yet a population claim (the cohort question is separate).

open_questions.question: Does the alpha-blocking ratio hold across the full eegmmidb cohort with matched montages?

reference_tools: R eeg-berger-eegmmidb recipe (this gallery) reaches the same conclusion; this is its Python counterpart via physiopy + BIDS
